reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of a periodic rectangular pulse train with period 48 points, robust-standardized amplitude ~2.47 (90th percentile), and near-zero baseline. Each cycle features a sharp vertical rise (~1–2 points wide) from baseline to peak, a flat-top plateau lasting ~36–38 points, and a sharp vertical fall (~1–2 points wide) back to baseline. The plateau exhibits minimal noise or drift—roughness and curvature are zero in catalog statistics—and the median is exactly zero across all candidates. Minor morphological variations exist: candidate 1 shows a slight negative slope per point (-0.017) across its 3-cycle span, while others are perfectly flat; candidate 3 (5 cycles) reveals subtle high-frequency ripple on plateau tops (<0.02 amplitude), likely quantization or residual noise, but no trend or distortion. All pulses align tightly in timing and shape across candidates, confirming stable cadence. Boundary truncation is absent—the pulses are fully contained within each window, and start/end points match expected phase (rise at index mod 48 ≈ 8–9). Acceptable variation includes negligible plateau waviness, tiny slope deviations (<0.02 per point), and consistent pulse width (~40 points total: ~2 up, ~36 flat, ~2 down). No sustained deviations, outliers, or irregular intervals occur across reliable candidates.
